newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dowa Mining says mulls raising copper capacity.
newsitem.headline: Dowa Mining says mulls raising copper capacity.

text.p: Dowa Mining Co Ltd said on Tuesday it was considering expanding copper refining capacity at its Kosaka plant in the near future.

A company spokeswoman said Dowa Mining might raise Kosaka's capacity to 6,000 tonnes per month from the current 5,000 to match its smelting capacity of 6,000. It might then increase smelting capacity as well.
Excess blister currently is sent to the Onahama smelter jointly owned by Dowa and five other Japanese copper companies.
The spokeswoman gave no further details, including the timing and costs of the capacity increase. She said the company would make a final decision by May 26, when it announces its 1996/97 results.
The expansion would follow an increase last August in Kosaka's electrolytic copper refining capacity to 5,000 tonnes per month from about 4,400 tonnes previously.
Dowa said at that time that it was considering a further lift in refining capacity to 6,000 tonnes.
In February the company said Akita Zinc Co, in which Dowa holds a majority stake, decided to boost capacity at its Iijima zinc smelter by a modest 20,000 tonnes per year.
